one_liner: ANSI C JSON DOM library beating RapidJSON via single-file design, in-situ parsing, and low-allocation strategy.
what_it_does: Parses and serializes JSON through a DOM API split into immutable read-side types (yyjson_doc/yyjson_val) and mutable build-side types (yyjson_mut_doc/yyjson_mut_val), with copy functions to convert between them. Ships as exactly one yyjson.h and one yyjson.c targeting ANSI C89 — the API is plain C accessor functions (yyjson_obj_get, yyjson_get_int, ...), not a drop-in for RapidJSON's C++ template DOM. Also supports JSON Pointer/Patch/Merge Patch, opt-in JSON5 features (comments, trailing commas), file and incremental readers, and accurate int64/uint64/double round-tripping.
how_it_is_fast: No explicit SIMD anywhere (ANSI C89 throughout); the README attributes speed instead to a modern-CPU-friendly code shape (high ILP, good branch prediction, tolerant of misaligned access) plus three concrete design choices visible in the docs: a single up-front memory allocation per document sized via yyjson_read_max_memory_usage rather than per-node mallocs, an optional in-situ reader (YYJSON_READ_INSITU) that parses strings in place inside the caller's buffer to skip copies, and a built-in fast float parse/print path that bypasses libc strtod/dtoa (toggle: YYJSON_DISABLE_FAST_FP_CONV). doc/Performance.md is a TODO stub, so no deeper algorithmic writeup exists in-repo.
when_to_use: Parsing/serializing JSON in a C or C++ codebase where RapidJSON is the current baseline and a plain-C DOM API is acceptable
Need strict int64/uint64/double round-trip fidelity and RFC 8259 conformance
Want to vendor one header + one source file with no build system, on ANSI C89 for portability (CI covers x86/arm/ppc/riscv/s390x/wasm with gcc/clang/msvc/tcc/watcom)
Can parse into a mutable buffer and use YYJSON_READ_INSITU to cut allocation/copy overhead
Need JSON Pointer/Patch/Merge Patch or opt-in JSON5 leniency (comments, trailing commas) built in
when_not_to_use: Access pattern is index/key lookup-heavy rather than sequential iteration — arrays/objects use a linked-list-like structure (README Limitations)
Need to mutate a document immediately after parsing — read results are immutable; requires yyjson_doc_mut_copy first
simdjson's On-Demand API applies (most fields known at compile time) — README states it beats yyjson there; this benchmark only covers DOM-vs-DOM
Cross-version ABI stability is required — 'Ensure ABI stability' is still an unchecked TODO in the README
Building/mutating one yyjson_mut_doc from multiple threads — mutable types are documented not thread-safe

integration.dependencies: none (ANSI C89, no explicit SIMD); optionally built as a static/shared lib via CMake
integration.min_toolchain: C89 (CI also builds under gcc, clang, msvc, tcc, watcom)
integration.platforms: x86, arm, ppc, riscv, s390x, wasm per CI matrix; no SIMD/CPU-feature requirement
integration.thread_safety: No global variables. yyjson_doc/yyjson_val (immutable, post-parse) are thread-safe for concurrent reads; yyjson_mut_doc/yyjson_mut_val (mutable, build-side) are not thread-safe.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different API paradigm (plain C accessor functions vs RapidJSON's C++ template DOM); same JSON-DOM concept, not source-compatible

gotchas: YYJSON_READ_INSITU requires a mutable, non-const buffer with extra padding bytes; passing a const string with this flag is a caller error
Parsed (immutable) docs can be edited via yyjson_set_* functions, but the README calls this 'breaking the immutable convention' and says to only do it from a single thread
Duplicate object keys are preserved, not deduped or rejected (README Limitations; issue #254 asking for a forbid-duplicates flag is still open)
Calling setlocale() concurrently with parsing can corrupt float parsing if the platform isn't IEEE-754 or YYJSON_DISABLE_FAST_FP_CONV is set (falls back to strtod)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick yyjson over simdjson when you want one portable ANSI C89 file with no SIMD/CPU-feature dependency and a DOM object you keep around (simdjson's DOM stringify trails at 0.61 vs yyjson's 1.51 GB/s on the EC2 table); pick simdjson instead when its On-Demand API fits or peak SIMD throughput outweighs portability. Pick yyjson over glaze when the codebase is C rather than C++, or you need a runtime dynamic DOM instead of glaze's reflection-based static-type serialization.
verified_claims_summary: On AWS EC2 (AMD EPYC 7R32, gcc 9.3, CMake Release build i.e. -O3 -DNDEBUG plus -march=native) yyjson(insitu) parses twitter.json at 1.80 GB/s and stringifies at 1.51 GB/s versus RapidJSON(insitu) 0.77 GB/s parse and RapidJSON(utf8) 0.26/0.39 GB/s parse/stringify, roughly 2.3x-6.9x. On Apple A14 (clang 12) yyjson reaches 2.39-3.51 GB/s parse versus RapidJSON's 0.30-0.75 GB/s.
